newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sees cautious grain export subsidy policy.
newsitem.headline: EU sees cautious grain export subsidy policy.

text.p: The European Union will have to pursue a cautious grain export subsidy policy for the rest of the 1996/97 (July-June) season because of budgetary problems, European Commission Director-General David Roberts said on Wednesday.

The current EU subsidy for wheat was about five times higher than the average level of 4.25 Ecus a tonne included in the draft 1997 budget, Roberts, who is in charge of international agricultural relations and the farm budget, told a grains conference .
"Therefore, we have every interest in seeing the refund fall rather than pursuing an aggressive subsidy policy involving an increase in refunds," he said.
He said grain stocks were set to increase during the current marketing season following a huge harvest. But he declined to give any figures.

The amount of land farmers would have to leave idle during the 1998 harvest campaign to qualify for EU aid payments was likely to be revised upwards substantially, Roberts also told the conference, organised by Agra Europe, a consultancy which publishes newsletters on EU affairs.
For the 1997 harvest, grain farmers must idle five percent of their farmland under a rotational set-aside scheme.
